q: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position (or) equilibrium line are called ____ respectively.
e: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position (or) equilibrium line are called wave crest and wave trough respectively. Wave crest and wave trough here means a travelling disturbance that carries energy, not the medium itself. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called ____.
e: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength. Wavelength here means the distance from one crest to the next crest. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is ____.
e: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is metre (m). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of ____.
e: Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of same phase. Same phase here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source is also called ____.
e: The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source is also called frequency. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The SI unit of frequency is ____.
e: The SI unit of frequency is hertz (Hz). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.
One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second. The physics in this sentence is built around one complete cycle per second.

q: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called ____ of a wave.
e: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called period of a wave. Period here means the time for one complete vibration.

q: The unit of period is the ____.
e: The unit of period is the second (s). The unit that belongs with this quantity is second (s).

q: The period is the ____ of the frequency.
e: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The amplitude of a wave is the ____ of displacement of vibrating particle.
e: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of vibrating particle. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: Velocity of wave is the ____ with which a wave crest travels.
e: Velocity of wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels. Speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The unit of wave velocity is ____.
e: The unit of wave velocity is metre per second ($\text{m s}^{-1}$). Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Most of the periodic waves are represented by ____ graphs.
e: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine (or) cosine graphs. The physics in this sentence is built around sine (or) cosine.

q: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave can be obtained by ____.
e: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave can be obtained by $v = f \lambda$. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.
